newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kuehne & Nagel Germany profits down 3.5pct.
newsitem.headline: Kuehne & Nagel Germany profits down 3.5pct.

text.p: Kuehne & Nagel (AG & Co), the German division of Swiss forwarder Kuehne & Nagel International AG, saw net profits fall 3.5 percent to 35.5 million Swiss francs ($24.2 million) last year.
Operating profits rose 1.3 percent to 397.9 million Sfr but turnover was 6.5 percent down at 1,958 million Sfr, the annual company report said.
The German airfreight division increased gross profits to 48.6 million Sfr on turnover of 337.5 million Sfr in 1996 after making profits of 46.1 million Sfr on turnover of 374.3 million Sfr in 1995.
Cornelius Geber, KN Germany chairman, told Reuters in an interview: "1996 was our best operational year in Germany ever."
The slight fall in net profits was generated by travel agency activities but freight forwarding had had a very successful year, he said.
KN was effectively the biggest international freight forwarder in Germany since rival Schenker (STHG.F) had split its divisions into separate companies, Geber said.
The firm was certainly the most profitable forwarder in Germany thanks to cost-cutting, new concepts and more active marketing, he added.
There were no plans to split operations into separate air, ocean, overland or logistics subsidiares since synergy effects and combined or multimodal products would be lost, Geber stressed.
Geber added: "In airfreight we grew very well last year, in contrast to most other forwarders in Germany, by about 10 percent."
Exports remained the main air cargo business but imports were becoming more important due to the relocation of production by German firms aboard, in particular to eastern Europe and Asia, he noted.
Ocean freight carried a record volume of 80,000 twenty foot equivalent container units (TEU) thanks to strong Far East and North America business.
Geber said the loss-making overland traffic division was being re-structured and a joint venture named Cargo Concept with 11 small forwarders had been launched.
This operated a new Germany overland hub in Bad Hersfeld and had improved distribution times within Germany, he pointed out.
"We believe we can stop the negative trend in land transport," he added.
Logistics would play an increasingly important role due to globalisation of production, Geber said.

In 1997, KN would invest 14 million marks alone in new communication systems this year, open a Cologne logistics terminal and target import business, he added. ($ = 1.466 Swiss Francs) - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
